gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Redragon's own US store sells the S136 combo (K628 75% tri-mode keyboard + M693 mouse, one shared 2.4 GHz dongle) open-box for $29.99, half its $59.99 new price; or that the Logitech MX Mechanical + MX Master 3S pair costs $269.98 bought separately on logitech.com today ($179.99 + $89.99), not the $279.98 mechkeyfoundry prints.
standout_why: I compared against keyboardverdict.com and mechkeyfoundry.com; deskfinds.com returned 403. keyboardverdict prices Redragon's S101M-KS and RedThunder K10 but not the S136, and gives the MX pair only as a '~$215-230' range. mechkeyfoundry already adds up the MX pair, at $279.98 using the older $99.99 mouse price, and gives the MX battery figures I meant to derive from: 15 days with backlight on and 70 days for the mouse. That leaves only price deltas as new, and they are small. I couldn't compute the angle's real number, the days a combo runs before the first device needs charging at a stated duty cycle, for any budget combo ChatGPT showed. Redragon's store rate-limited every product-page request (HTTP 429), and its PDF manual wouldn't parse.
decides: It only confirms the budget pick and doesn't decide anything. The S136 is the one ChatGPT-shown combo I could price at the maker today: $59.99 new, or $29.99 open-box from the same store. Without sourced battery hours for the K628 and M693 I can't rank it against the S168 or BS8773 on days between charges. That runtime comparison would be the deciding figure if a later pass can open the Redragon spec pages.
